title: P35: RMS-normalized queries and keys with a learned per-head gain (QK-norm) in all five blocks
description: P35 on top of incumbent 051-claude: every block RMS-normalizes q and k over each 32-dim head and multiplies q by a learned per-head gain initialized to 2.0 (initial max |logit| 11.3), in pretraining, RL and evaluation alike, adding 40 parameters and leaving all other initial weights bitwise equal per seed. Decoupling attention sharpness from the growing norms of W_q and W_k (as in OLMo 2, Gemma 3 and the Muon-trained modded-nanogpt speedruns) should give a better-conditioned pretrained model per step and keep the frozen AdamW expert-iteration fine-tuning from sharpening attention onto the cap-6 patterns, so RL starts from and keeps a more adaptable model.
hypothesis: Mechanism: without QK-norm, attention logits scale with |W_q||W_k|, so every Muon update to the q/k projections (fixed spectral-norm steps) also changes attention temperature; logits can grow quadratically in weight scale and heads saturate early (attention entropy collapse, Zhai et al. 2023, ICML, 'Stabilizing Transformer Training by Preventing Attention Entropy Collapse'). With q and k normalized, only the direction of q and k sets which key wins and one learned scalar per head sets how sharply, which OLMo 2 (2024/2025, arXiv 2501.00656), Gemma 3 (2025) and modded-nanogpt (2024-2025, Muon plus QK-norm) use for more stable, faster optimization at equal steps. Expected effects here: (1) in a 300 s, ~2300-step pretraining run, lower or equal validation loss at matched steps despite slightly fewer steps; (2) during the fixed RL stage (AdamW on all parameters, 4 expert-iteration rounds on the model's own proofs), attention cannot sharpen through weight-norm growth, which should reduce overfitting of attention patterns to the round's accepted (mostly 7-line) proofs and keep the model able to extend the length frontier each round, so round-2..4 targets solved and the 9-10-line dev solves improve relative to 051 (151/126/166 at 9-10 lines per seed). Alternative outcomes: (a) the bounded initial sharpness (max logit 11.3 unless q_gain grows; AdamW moves it about 1e-3 per step) blurs exact line-citation lookup in long prompts, raising invalid samples and lowering the metric (negative); (b) the model is too small and short-trained for logit growth to matter, so the effect is ~0; (c) fp32 normalization cost lowers throughput enough to cost pretraining quality; (d) 051's 286.33 (288/260/311) may be a lucky draw: every one of the six later attempts on the five-layer incumbent scored 239-277, so the bar is high; (e) single-seed sd ~44. Data, tokenizer, RL, evaluation, seeds and budgets are unchanged; the QK-norm architecture persists into RL and evaluation because it is part of the model. Only the fixed three-seed downstream mean decides.
expected_delta: Central prediction -10 to +20 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 versus incumbent 051-claude exact mean 286.333333 (288/260/311); plausible downside -40 if bounded logits blur citation lookup. Expect pretraining steps a few percent below 051's 2320-2370, final val loss within +-0.006 of 051 (0.0924/0.0951/0.0932), held-out greedy 0.975-0.992, learned q_gain mostly above its 2.0 init by the end of pretraining, and per-seed totals about 950-1150 s (051: 1053/957/941 s).

arch.pos: rope (base 10000), applied to the normalized q and k
arch.change: P35 QK-norm, one mechanism: every block's class is swapped in place to QKNormBlock, whose attn is the fork's Block.attn except that q and k are RMS-normalized over each 32-dim head (fp32, eps 1e-6, no learned weight) and q is then multiplied by a learned per-head gain q_gain of shape (8,1,1) initialized to QK_GAIN = 2.0, before RoPE and before the KV cache write; both are cast back to v's dtype. SDPA keeps its default 1/sqrt(32) scale, so the initial max |logit| is 2.0*sqrt(32) = 11.3 (standard-scale QK-norm at head dim 128) and random-init logit std is 2.0. 5 blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads, d_ff 1024, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout and every other setting identical to 051-claude.
arch.n_params_detail: 051's 4,000,000 (per block 789,760; 5 blocks 3,948,800 + emb 25,344 + head 25,344 + ln_f 512) + 5 blocks x 8 q_gain = 4,000,040 (counted locally with the fork's GPT)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork, swap each block's __class__ to pretrain.QKNormBlock and add q_gain = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(8,1,1)), then load the state dict (it has blocks.i.q_gain keys, so the plain fork GPT will not load it strictly)
arch.kv_cache: one fork-format KV-cache dict per block (5 per sample); caches hold normalized, gained, rotated keys; cached prefill+decode matched the full forward to 1.4e-6 locally (fork block: 1.1e-6)

qk_norm.where: per head, over head_dim 32, before RoPE, all 5 blocks, in pretraining, RL and eval
qk_norm.q_gain: learned scalar per head per block (40 params), init 2.0
qk_norm.precision: normalization in fp32, result cast to v's dtype (bf16 under autocast)

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) are in Muon. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases, LayerNorm parameters and the 5 new q_gain tensors (8,1,1) throughout, at the auxiliary AdamW lr/wd 0.1; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW (q_gain is 3-D, so the ndim==2 Muon selection excludes it). The frozen RL AdamW trains all 4,000,040 parameters including q_gain.
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: 051-claude's rule with bitwise-identical initial weights per seed by construction (the class swap and torch.full draw no RNG; they run after the orthogonal init): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter with gain 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0; new q_gain = 2.0 everywhere. No reinitialization during RL.
config.timing: not benchmarked on A40; the fp32 normalization of q and k adds elementwise work on (B,8,T,32) tensors per block, so expect a few percent fewer pretraining steps than 051's 2320-2370 and slightly slower decode
